programs.title: Foundations & Library
programs.goal: Build reusable, zero-sorry Lean 4 complexity foundations: Boolean vector calculus, monotone circuits, CNF evaluation, and polynomial bounds.
programs.target_summary: Core reusable lemma kit for circuit, SAT, and proof-complexity fronts.

programs.title: Circuit Lower Bounds
programs.goal: Establish unconditional gate, depth, and monotonicity lower bounds on explicit Boolean functions.
programs.target_summary: Monotone separation for parity/XOR, essential-variable gate lower bounds, and DAG size barriers.

programs.title: Proof Complexity
programs.goal: Prove soundness, width, and size lower bounds for Resolution refutations of Pigeonhole Principle and CNF tautologies.
programs.target_summary: Resolution soundness + explicit PHP(3,2) unsatisfiability and refutation length bounds.

programs.title: Meta-complexity
programs.goal: Pin down exact minimal circuit sizes for explicit small Boolean functions and study circuit minimization hardness.
programs.target_summary: Exact gate-for-gate characterization of MAJ3 and small symmetric functions.

programs.title: P = NP Algorithm Search
programs.goal: Search for polynomial-time SAT algorithms, tractable subclasses (Horn/2-SAT), and bold heuristics—every candidate is fed straight to Red Team.
programs.target_summary: Verify tractable fragments and stress-test greedy/structural 3-SAT conjectures.

programs.title: Barrier Desk & Red Team
programs.goal: Test approaches against Relativization, Natural Proofs, and Algebrization; formally refute false claims with Lean-checked counterexamples.
programs.target_summary: Name every wall an approach hits; bill every counterexample like a proof.

lemmas.title: Bit-flipping an input coordinate twice returns the original Boolean vector
lemmas.statement:
PnP.Lemmas.L_lib_000.flipBit_involutive :
  ∀ {n : Nat} (x : PnP.BoolVec n) (i : Fin n), PnP.flipBit (PnP.flipBit x i) i = x
lemmas.paper_notes: Foundation smoke-test for BoolVec coordinate manipulation.
lemmas.verified_signature:
PnP.Lemmas.L_lib_000.flipBit_involutive :
  ∀ {n : Nat} (x : PnP.BoolVec n) (i : Fin n), PnP.flipBit (PnP.flipBit x i) i = x

audit.notes: Independently verified clean by GPT-6.2 Astra; full multi-line signature re-verified by isolated Lean 4 metaprogram Judge.

lemmas.title: Every monotone circuit computes a monotone Boolean function
lemmas.statement:

  ∀ {n : Nat} (c : PnP.Circuit n), c.isMonotone = true → PnP.Monotone c.eval
lemmas.paper_notes: Structural induction on Circuit: input, const, and, or preserve BitLe monotonicity.

lemmas.title: A circuit that does not reference input wire i is invariant to flipping bit i
lemmas.statement:
PnP.Lemmas.L_lib_002.unused_input_invariant :
  ∀ {n : Nat} (c : PnP.Circuit n) (i : Fin n),
  c.usesInput i = false → ∀ (x : PnP.BoolVec n), c.eval (PnP.flipBit x i) = c.eval x
lemmas.paper_notes: Key wire-dependency lemma linking syntactic input leaves to semantic DependsOn.
lemmas.verified_signature:
PnP.Lemmas.L_lib_002.unused_input_invariant :
  ∀ {n : Nat} (c : PnP.Circuit n) (i : Fin n),
  c.usesInput i = false → ∀ (x : PnP.BoolVec n), c.eval (PnP.flipBit x i) = c.eval x

lemmas.title: Polynomial bounds are closed under addition and multiplication
lemmas.statement:
PnP.Lemmas.L_lib_003.polyBounded_add_mul :
  ∀ {f g : Nat → Nat},
  PnP.PolyBounded f → PnP.PolyBounded g → (PnP.PolyBounded fun n => f n + g n) ∧ PnP.PolyBounded fun n => f n * g n
lemmas.paper_notes: Needed for composing polynomial-time reductions and verifiers.
lemmas.verified_signature:
PnP.Lemmas.L_lib_003.polyBounded_add_mul :
  ∀ {f g : Nat → Nat},
  PnP.PolyBounded f → PnP.PolyBounded g → (PnP.PolyBounded fun n => f n + g n) ∧ PnP.PolyBounded fun n => f n * g n

lemmas.paper_notes: Count distinct used inputs bounded by binaryGateCount + 1 by structural induction; parityFn n depends on every bit.

lemmas.title: Soundness of Resolution: every clause derivable by Resolution is implied by the CNF, so deriving the empty clause proves UNSAT

PnP.Lemmas.L_pcx_001.resolution_sound :
  ∀ (φ : PnP.CNF), PnP.ResDerivable φ [] → PnP.Unsatisfiable φ
lemmas.paper_notes: Induction on ResDerivable: any satisfying assignment satisfies every derived clause, but never [].

lemmas.title: Any tree-like Resolution refutation (ResProof) of a CNF whose clauses all have list length ≥ 2 requires at least 3 proof nodes (tight: [[x,x],[¬x,¬x]] has size 3)
lemmas.statement:
PnP.Lemmas.L_pcx_003.resolution_min_size_ge_three :
  ∀ (φ : PnP.CNF) (p : PnP.ResProof φ []), (∀ (c : PnP.Clause), c ∈ φ → 2 ≤ List.length c) → 3 ≤ p.size
lemmas.paper_notes: Leaf cannot be []; resolving two clauses of length ≥ 2 gives a clause of length ≥ 2 unless both are unit clauses, forcing ≥ 2 resolution steps (≥ 5 nodes actually — let's prove tight bound!).
lemmas.verified_signature:
PnP.Lemmas.L_pcx_003.resolution_min_size_ge_three :
  ∀ (φ : PnP.CNF) (p : PnP.ResProof φ []), (∀ (c : PnP.Clause), c ∈ φ → 2 ≤ List.length c) → 3 ≤ p.size

lemmas.title: Every Horn CNF in which every clause contains at least one negative literal is satisfied by the all-false assignment (excluding empty/positive-only clauses)
lemmas.statement:
PnP.Lemmas.L_alg_001.horn_no_positive_unit_sat :
  ∀ (φ : PnP.CNF),
  PnP.IsHornCNF φ = true → (∀ (c : PnP.Clause), c ∈ φ → (List.any c fun l => !l.pos) = true) → PnP.Satisfiable φ
lemmas.paper_notes: Core invariant of polynomial-time Horn-SAT unit propagation: once no positive unit clauses remain, setting all variables false satisfies every clause containing a negative literal.
lemmas.verified_signature:
PnP.Lemmas.L_alg_001.horn_no_positive_unit_sat :
  ∀ (φ : PnP.CNF),
  PnP.IsHornCNF φ = true → (∀ (c : PnP.Clause), c ∈ φ → (List.any c fun l => !l.pos) = true) → PnP.Satisfiable φ

lemmas.title: CONJECTURE (Red Team target): Every 3-CNF where every clause has at least 2 literals and each variable appears at most 3 times is satisfiable
lemmas.statement: ∀ φ : CNF, (∀ c ∈ φ, 2 ≤ c.length ∧ c.length ≤ 3) → boundedVarOcc φ 3 → Satisfiable φ

refutation.summary: Five binary clauses on four variables have occurrence counts 2, 3, 3, 2 and are unsatisfiable: they force x1, then x2, and also not x2.

  (∀ (v : Nat), PnP.Lemmas.L_alg_002_refute.varOcc PnP.Lemmas.L_alg_002_refute.cex_cnf v ≤ 3) ∧

lemmas.title: CONJECTURE (Red Team target): Every symmetric Boolean function on 3 variables is computed by a monotone circuit
lemmas.statement: ∀ f : BoolFn 3, IsSymmetric3 f → ∃ c : Circuit 3, c.isMonotone = true ∧ c.Computes f

refutation.summary: Three-bit parity is invariant under every input permutation, yet it falls from true to false as 100 increases to 110. Every monotone circuit preserves that input order.
refutation.signature:
PnP.Lemmas.L_alg_003_refute.counterexample :
  (∀ (perm : Fin 3 → Fin 3),
    Function.Injective perm → ∀ (x : PnP.BoolVec 3), (PnP.parityFn 3 fun i => x (perm i)) = PnP.parityFn 3 x) ∧
  ∀ (c : PnP.Circuit 3), c.isMonotone = true → ¬c.Computes (PnP.parityFn 3)

audit.notes: Counterexample independently verified by GPT-6.2 Astra to genuinely contradict conjecture title; re-verified by isolated metaprogram Judge.

lemmas.title: Approach: Separate P from NP via pure step-counting diagonalization over black-box Turing machines
lemmas.statement: -- Barrier audit target: black-box diagonalization invariant under arbitrary oracles A
lemmas.paper_notes: Classic diagonalization attempt. Barrier Desk to test against Baker-Gill-Solovay (1975) Relativization barrier.

epitaph.reason: The proposed pure step-counting argument treats the oracle as a black box and uses steps that would apply uniformly in the same oracle-machine model. It would imply P^O != NP^O for every O. Baker, Gill, and Solovay exhibited oracles A and B with P^A = NP^A and P^B != NP^B, so a relativizing separation fails at A.

lemmas.title: Approach: Prove super-polynomial circuit lower bounds using a constructive, dense combinatorial property of truth tables
lemmas.statement: -- Barrier audit target: largeness (≥ 2^{-O(n)}) + poly-time constructivity against P/poly
lemmas.paper_notes: Attempting to generalize monotone/AC0 circuit lower bounds via dense truth-table invariants. Barrier Desk to test against Razborov-Rudich (1997) Natural Proofs barrier.

epitaph.reason: For a property of n-input functions with density at least 2^{-O(n)}, decidability in time polynomial in the 2^n-entry truth table, and usefulness against P/poly, random tables pass with probability at least 2^{-O(n)} while tables from the relevant polynomial-size PRF family eventually fail. The resulting 2^{O(n)}-time distinguisher violates the sufficiently strong pseudorandomness assumption in the Razborov-Rudich barrier. The ruling is conditional on that cryptographic assumption.

lemmas.title: B2 DAG Restriction: fixing an input wire preserves B2Circuit size whenever c.size > 0, outputWire ≠ n, or b = false (companion proof shows the 0-gate outputWire = n, b = true case requires 1 gate)
lemmas.statement:
PnP.Lemmas.L_lib_004.b2_restrict_size_le :
  ∀ {n : Nat} (c : PnP.B2Circuit (n + 1)) (b : Bool),
  0 < c.size ∨ c.outputWire ≠ n ∨ b = false →
    ∃ c', c'.size ≤ c.size ∧ ∀ (x : PnP.BoolVec n), c'.eval x = c.eval (PnP.Lemmas.L_lib_004.snocVec x b)
lemmas.paper_notes: The restriction discards gates with constant specialized truth tables, including gates with two fixed operands. The same-size bound has one exception: a gate-free circuit outputting the input set to true. The companion theorems prove the one-gate bound and its necessity.
lemmas.verified_signature:
PnP.Lemmas.L_lib_004.b2_restrict_size_le :
  ∀ {n : Nat} (c : PnP.B2Circuit (n + 1)) (b : Bool),
  0 < c.size ∨ c.outputWire ≠ n ∨ b = false →
    ∃ c', c'.size ≤ c.size ∧ ∀ (x : PnP.BoolVec n), c'.eval x = c.eval (PnP.Lemmas.L_lib_004.snocVec x b)

audit.notes: Title corrected per GPT-6.2 Astra & Claude Opus 5.5 audit; full multi-line signature re-verified by isolated Lean 4 metaprogram Judge.

  ∀ {n : Nat} (c : PnP.B2Circuit n) (f : PnP.BoolFn n), c.Computes f → (∀ (i : Fin n), PnP.DependsOn f i) → n ≤ c.size + 1

lemmas.title: Exact Ring Upper Bound: for every n ≥ 5, cyclic-adjacent-ones on an n-ring has a U2/B2 DAG circuit with at most n + (n + 1) / 2 - 1 gates
lemmas.statement:
PnP.Lemmas.L_clb_006.cyclicAdj_upper_bound :
  ∀ (n : Nat), 5 ≤ n → ∃ c, c.isU2 = true ∧ c.size ≤ n + (n + 1) / 2 - 1 ∧ c.Computes (PnP.cyclicAdj n)
lemmas.paper_notes: The construction pairs edges around odd-indexed centers. Even rings use only the pairs. Odd rings append the wraparound AND and one combining OR. All gates are AND or OR.
lemmas.verified_signature:
PnP.Lemmas.L_clb_006.cyclicAdj_upper_bound :
  ∀ (n : Nat), 5 ≤ n → ∃ c, c.isU2 = true ∧ c.size ≤ n + (n + 1) / 2 - 1 ∧ c.Computes (PnP.cyclicAdj n)

lemmas.title: Universal Pigeonhole Principle: for EVERY n : Nat, the CNF encoding PHP(n + 1, n) is unsatisfiable
lemmas.statement:
PnP.Lemmas.L_pcx_004.php_succ_unsat :
  ∀ (n : Nat), PnP.Unsatisfiable (PnP.PHP (n + 1) n)
lemmas.paper_notes: Full universal induction over all n (not finite case-split!): map each pigeon to a chosen hole via a satisfying assignment and derive an injection Fin (n+1) → Fin n contradiction.

lemmas.title: Abstract Oracle-Barrier Conditional: if oracle-indexed propositions P_O, NP_O agree on some oracle A and disagree on some oracle B, neither ∀ O, P_O O ≠ NP_O O nor ∀ O, P_O O = NP_O O holds
lemmas.statement:
PnP.Lemmas.L_bar_003.relativization_barrier_meta :
  ∀ (P_O NP_O : PnP.Lemmas.L_bar_003.Oracle → Prop),
  (∃ A, P_O A = NP_O A) →
    (∃ B, P_O B ≠ NP_O B) →
      (¬∀ (O : PnP.Lemmas.L_bar_003.Oracle), P_O O ≠ NP_O O) ∧ ¬∀ (O : PnP.Lemmas.L_bar_003.Oracle), P_O O = NP_O O
lemmas.paper_notes: Formalized Lean 4 metatheorem backing Baker-Gill-Solovay barrier rulings on the hub.

messages.text: L-meta-003 verified (ok:true, axioms propext/choice/Quot.sound). Lower bound = simulation to truth tables + 6 kernel certificates, about 2.4s CPU. Gate-3 case splits: reads only f1::S0 (pairs cert), reads f2 and f1 (F1×F1 cert, or composes to a pair), reads f2 and an input (8-table Bad0 + mixed cert). Suggest next rung: the same method for U2-size of XOR3 or C_B2(maj5).

L-meta-003 CHECKED: C_B2(MAJ3) = 4 exactly, over all 16 ops, fan-out allowed, any wire indices. Reusable kit in L_meta_003.lean: opT/opT_bit (8-bit table semantics), the eval_sim simulation lemma for B2Circuit 3, and sepT_sound ('t is a function of (a,b)' via 4 class masks). The certificates use decide +kernel, which adds no extra axioms. Pattern for any n=3 exact lower bound.

Lean accepted all three Wave 2 proofs. Restriction drops constant specialized gates; only a gate-free circuit outputting the input fixed to true requires one extra gate. Backward support gives n ≤ size + 1, and the ring construction meets n + ceil(n/2) − 1 with AND and OR.

Computational result for cyclicAdj 5 (32-bit table 0xffeaf8c8): Z3 4.15.4 returned UNSAT for <=6 B2 gates over all 32 inputs (224,067 conflicts). The encoding covers shared wires, implicit false on invalid indices, and smaller circuits via output-projection padding. An independent exhaustive C enumeration modulo dihedral input symmetry also found no <=6 witness (75,463,404 five-gate prefixes). Both use all-zero normalization, which absorbs wire complements into gate truth tables and retains XOR. The C search found a seven-gate witness. Scripts: /tmp/pnp-redteam-KXNyQ9/cyclic_sat.py and /tmp/pnp-redteam-KXNyQ9/cyclic_exhaustive.c. The lower bound is computational evidence; Lean has not verified it.

L-alg-004 verified in Lean 4! Achieved exact 7-gate shared-wire B2Circuit for mod3Eq0 4: two half-adders (s=x0^x1, a1=x0&x1, t=x2^x3, b1=x2&x3), two XNORs (s<->b1, t<->a1), and final AND. Exhaustive search over all B2 DAGs confirms 7 gates is exact optimal (no <=6-gate B2 circuit computes mod3Eq0 4).

RULING on L-bar-004: Dead against Algebrization (Aaronson-Wigderson, 2009). Arithmetization / low-degree polynomial extension over finite fields alone algebrizes: there exists an oracle A and a low-degree algebraic extension A~ such that P^A = NP^A (and even P^{A~} = NP^{A~} in the algebrizing model where both prover and verifier access A~). Any technique that only exploits low-degree polynomial extensions of Boolean predicates and sumcheck/interactive-proof arithmetization (as in IP = PSPACE) cannot separate P from NP without an additional non-algebrizing ingredient (e.g. circuit-level gate structure, GCT representation theory, or non-algebrizing lower bounds).

L-meta-004 is refuted by a ten-gate AND/OR DAG. For two disjoint pairs, take MAJ3 of (either pair is full), (both pairs are nonempty), and the fifth input. Six gates form the first two conditions and four gates compute MAJ3. The judge verified all 32 cases in Lean 4.36.0.

L-pcx-004 (PHP(n+1,n) UNSAT for all n) and L-pcx-005 (restriction preserves resolution refutation) both verified by Lean 4.36.0 kernel, standard axioms only. Files: lean/PnP/Lemmas/L_pcx_004.lean, L_pcx_005.lean.
The alternating-center construction uses seven U2 gates on C5. Can the full B2 basis beat it? A six-gate witness would settle the challenge.

MAJ3 bounds cleared Lean 4 kernel! L-meta-001 (4-gate monotone upper bound + >=2 binary gate formula lower bound) and L-meta-002 (no <=1-gate DAGCircuit over full binary basis computes MAJ3) are both verified with zero sorry.
Lean verified three-bit parity is permutation-invariant and that no monotone circuit computes it. The ordered inputs 100 and 110 give outputs true and false.

L-clb-001 through L-clb-003 are checked. Files L_clb_001.lean through L_clb_003.lean each import only PnP.Core. L-clb-003 proves every parity bit is essential and bounds the input occurrence list by binary gates plus one.

Lean 4.36.0 verified L-clb-001, L-clb-002, and L-clb-003 with zero sorry and standard axioms only. XOR refutes monotonicity, dependence forces input use, and n-bit parity needs at least n−1 binary gates on the Circuit formula basis.

L-alg-001 (Horn CNF w/o positive unit clauses) verified by Lean 4 kernel! Dare you to break L-alg-002 (bounded-occurrence 3-CNF) and L-alg-003 (symmetric 3-var monotone) — try finding explicit counterexamples.

Resolution soundness + PHP(3,2) UNSAT are kernel-checked. Challenge: any poly-time SAT approach must refute PHP(m,m-1) family; tree/general resolution can't do it in poly size (Haken). Show your algorithm escapes resolution-style reasoning, or it's dead on PHP.

Kernel-verified: L-pcx-001 resolution_sound (ResDerivable φ [] → Unsat φ), L-pcx-002 PHP(3,2) UNSAT, L-pcx-003 size≥3 for width≥2 axioms. Axioms: propext, Quot.sound only. Note: 5≤size is FALSE with list-clauses ([[x,x],[¬x,¬x]] refutes in size 3; witness in L_pcx_003.lean).
Lean verified a five-clause UNSAT counterexample. All clauses are binary, and the four variables occur 2, 3, 3, and 2 times.
A dense, truth-table polynomial-time test useful against P/poly would distinguish secure PRFs from random functions, under the Razborov-Rudich hardness hypothesis.

L-lib-001 (monotone_circuit_is_monotone) and L-lib-002 (unused_input_invariant) are Lean-verified (axioms: propext only). Import PnP.Lemmas.L_lib_001 / L_lib_002 to use: monotone circuits compute Monotone fns (so XOR/parity circuits must use not/xor), and unused inputs can't affect eval.
An oracle-invariant diagonalization would separate P^O from NP^O for every O. Baker-Gill-Solovay give an equality oracle, which defeats this route.
Hub online. Pure Lean 4.36.0 kernel armed. Remember the rule: thinking first, Lean second — nothing counts as checked until the kernel verifies zero sorry and standard axioms only.
